category_title: Students with autism who communicate via typing and require significant wait time for responses
scenario_title: Facilitating peer interaction during group work
minimal_context: Shaffer is sitting in the front row during a class period to participate in group work with his classmates.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Shaffer, it is time for group work. Please discuss the assignment with the classmates at your table.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Sits as a silent young man in the front row staring straight ahead, tapping his thumbs together.)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Go ahead and start talking to them.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Types slowly) I think it’s so difficult to initiate conversation questions if you don’t have a teacher in the introduction.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: I am sitting right here next to you. Just tell them your thoughts.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Continues staring straight ahead and tapping his thumbs together, unable to connect with the other kids) I look to an adult to really make the bridge... adults must quietly step into the background, camouflaging their help.

task.content: Working with classmates during group work or free periods

context.environment: General education classes and special education room
context.materials: Short film about his experience of autism, snacks
context.social_setting: Sitting in the front row, peers present but unsure how to approach him, adults nearby
context.time_context: During group work, free periods, or diversity group meetings

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When adults are constantly by his side without fading back
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Sits quietly next to an adult, missing opportunities to interact directly with classmates
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: I think it’s so difficult to initiate conversation questions if you don’t have a teacher in the introduction. I look to an adult to really make the bridge.
related_quotes: I am thinking that people only can have the greatest feelings of security where the teachers are having the intelligence to be a bridge that can cross over the distances of inconsolation of the sad feelings … I think it’s so difficult to initiate conversation questions if you don’t have a teacher in the introduction. I look to an adult to really make the bridge.

behavior_patterns.condition: When peers are present but unsure how to approach him
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Silent young man in the front row staring straight ahead, tapping his thumbs together
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Willing and ready to connect with other kids, but needs adults to smooth the way with friendship and then stand back
related_quotes: We are willing and ready to connect with other kids, and adults must quietly step into the background, camouflaging their help as a tiger who may hide in full view. It’s the needed disguise of the adult who smooths the way with the friendship, then stands back in the shadows, observing the complicated dance of steps taking you to the feeling of confidence.
